items.title: TastyIgniter permits Path Traversal in Media Upload
items.description:
### Summary
Arbitrary file write outside `media/uploads/`

### Details

- upload a image but in the request, change the path from `/` to `/../../`.

```http
items.title: TastyIgniter allows Remote Code Execution (RCE) via Unrestricted file upload in Media Manager
items.description:
### Summary
Media manager accepts `.htaccess` file which can be used to perform RCE.

### Details
The file upload functionality from media manager somehow accepts `.htaccess` file. This file could be used to allow any extension to run PHP command. By doing so, it is possible to perform RCE.

### PoC
- Login as Admin
- Create a `.htaccess` file with the following code.

```
<FilesMatch "\.jpg$">
    SetHandler application/x-httpd-php
</FilesMatch>
```
- Upload the `.htaccess` file via the Media Manager.

Request
```
POST /admin/media_manager HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8888
Content-Length: 357
sec-ch-ua-platform: "Linux"
X-CSRF-TOKEN: 2vv3ZKpvfj2SkbbJzqmf8G053mNXqPLktxqd5eMx
Cache-Control: no-cache
Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9
sec-ch-ua: "Not-A.Brand";v="24", "Chromium";v="146"
sec-ch-ua-mobile: ?0
X-IGNITER-FILEUPLOAD: mediamanager
X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0

items.title: TastyIgniter mail template editor allows remote code execution via server-side template injection
items.description:
### Summary
**Where:** `POST /admin/mail_templates/edit/{id}` → body field  
**Who can trigger:** Any admin user with `Admin.MailTemplates` permission  
**Impact:** Arbitrary PHP execution on the server — full RCE

### Details
The Mail templates is vulnerable to SSTI and did not perform an validation and sanitization.

### PoC

- login as admin
- create new mail template with following command

```
@php echo shell_exec('echo "RCE Executed";id'); @endphp
```  

- save the request
- execute the request using `X-IGNITER-REQUEST-HANDLER: onTestTemplate`

items.title: fulgur allows Unbounded string-set value accumulation causes memory/CPU exhaustion (denial of service)
items.description:
`fulgur` converts untrusted HTML/CSS into PDF, commonly on a server that
processes input supplied by many tenants. In versions from 0.4.4 up to (but not
including) the patched release, the CSS `string-set` named-string values
resolved from a document were accumulated per element with no memory budget,
letting a small crafted document amplify into large retained memory (and the CPU
to copy it) — a denial of service.

A `string-set` value is attacker-controlled: it is resolved from an element's
own text (`content(text)`), from one of its attributes (`attr(...)`), or from a
CSS string literal. fulgur accumulated these values per element in two unbounded
places:

1. **Store (default path).** For every element that matches a `string-set` rule,
   fulgur pushes a copy of the resolved value into a store that is retained for
   the whole render and cloned again downstream into a per-node lookup

items.title: livewire-powergrid: SQL injection via sortDirection in naturalSort queries
items.description:
## [Description]

The public Livewire property `sortDirection` is interpolated **verbatim** into a
raw SQL `ORDER BY` clause and is not restricted to `asc`/`desc`, allowing arbitrary
SQL injection through `POST /livewire/update`.

**Data flow**

- **Source** — `src/Concerns/Sorting.php`: `public string $sortDirection;` is a
  Livewire-bound property with no whitelist/validation (it is only assigned and
  flipped by `reverseSort()`), so it is fully attacker-controlled via the standard
  Livewire update endpoint.
- **Taint** — `src/DataSource/Processors/Database/Pipelines/ColumnRawQueries.php`,
  `resolvePlaceholders()`:
  ```php
  preg_replace_callback('/\{(\w+)\}/', fn ($m) => data_get($this->component, $m[1], ''), $sql);
  ```
  substitutes `{sortDirection}` with the raw property value.
- **Sink** — `src/DataSource/Support/Sql.php::getSortSqlByDriver()` builds the
  `naturalSort` expres

items.title: laradocs  Command injection via unescaped Node.js binary path in KaTeX SSR
items.description:
### Summary
Local command injection (CWE-78) in server-side KaTeX rendering via an unescaped Node.js binary path in a `proc_open()` command string.

### Affected versions
>= 0.4.0, < 1.0.0

### Patched versions
>= 1.0.0 (fixed in commit `100cb1e`)

### Impact
When rendering KaTeX math **server-side**, Laradocs invoked Node via `proc_open()` with a command string in which the Node binary argument was not passed through `escapeshellarg()`.

`MarkdownPipelineFactory` constructs `KatexExtension` with the configured binary, which the render path resolved as:

```php
$node = $this->nodeBin ?? 'node';
$cmd = $node . ' ' . escapeshellarg($tmpFile) . ' ' . escapeshellarg($input);
```

`$this->nodeBin` comes from `Config::nullableString('laradocs.parser.katex.node_bin')`. Both possible sources — the configured `node_bin` value, or the `'node'` default resolved from `PATH` — are operator-controlled

items.title: @waline/client vulnerable to stored XSS through unsanitized comment edit previews
items.description:
### Summary

`@waline/client` renders the comment editor's live preview with `marked` and no sanitizer (`utils/markdown.ts`), and the preview is injected with `v-html`.

When a comment is edited, the editor is seeded with the comment's raw, un-sanitized body (`orig`).

Only administrators and the comment owner can edit. So an administrator who clicks Edit on an attacker's comment renders that attacker's raw HTML in their own session: an unauthenticated commenter achieves privilege-escalation stored XSS against a moderator with a single Edit click.

### Details

`packages/client/src/utils/markdown.ts:18-37` renders markdown with `marked` and returns the raw HTML with no sanitization (the client bundles no DOMPurify):

```ts

```
